title: The Tenth of Twenty-Four
status: Historical actor — last placed falling fifty feet from the castle wall after escaping the dragon's vacuum, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; survival not confirmed by the record
summary: Sir Frankfurt is the Hammer Bro the assault record leaves standing in a room Bowser had told him to guard, after the order to leave it had been given and had not reached him. When the supplied dragon put its head through the wall and asked where Bowser was, he answered it in Draconic. Since he was not the target, he said, perhaps he could be released. Then he told the dragon his family history, and the dragon began to suck him into its vacuum.
description:
The record gives the family history in full, because the dragon had to sit through it. Sir Frankfurt is the fourteenth of his name, or the fiftieth, depending on which end of the count he reaches first, and the tenth child of twenty-four. His father charged Mario and died before the third world was over. His mother died of grief a few days afterward. Bowser took in the surviving children. Bowser could be harsh, Sir Frankfurt said, but he had done right by them — which is the sentence that explains why a Hammer Bro stayed at a post everyone else had been told to abandon.

The dragon called the speech nonsense and began to suck him into its vacuum. The record is specific about how he got out: he grabbed the intake, curled into his shell and spun; the shell struck the machine, vaulted upward, overshot the landing, and fell from the fifty-foot castle. The record drops him 'into the unknown' and does not pick him up again. The dragon, it adds, was more shocked by the story than by the escape.

He is filed under the name he gave the dragon when it asked. The archive notes that a Hammer Bro who speaks the language of the thing that is eating him, and uses it to negotiate, is the kind of soldier a kingdom finds out it had only after the kingdom has fallen on him.

name: Fred (Hammer Bro)
title: The One Who Asked About the Switch
status: Historical actor — carried into a side room under Bowser's arm when the throne-room wall burst, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; placed with the king at the breach thereafter
summary: Fred is one of the two Hammer Bros Bowser carried out of the throne room 'the way a king carries equipment that has become unexpectedly alive' when the dragon finally brought the wall in. In the side room the two of them asked the question the rest of the night turned on: did the castle have a self-destruct switch, and if the dragon was taking it anyway, why not blow it up and walk the survivors to Neo Bowser City? The record does not say which of them asked it first.
description:
Bowser's answer was 'You want me to blow up my own castle?' The Hammer Bros' position, which the record preserves, was that Mario had once pressed a switch and brought a whole castle down, so the technology plainly existed; Bowser had not built such a switch, so if there was one here perhaps somebody had sabotaged it, and the argument drifted toward the axe at the end of the river. The archive files the proposal under Fred and the objections under Ed because it needs two articles for two Hammer Bros and one argument; take the split as filing, not testimony. The hag Bowser met a few minutes later turned out to have built a switch, and could not say what it did.

Fred is filed because the record files the question, and because the question was the first time that night anyone proposed treating the castle as a thing to be spent rather than a thing to be held. Bowser refused it. The refusal is in the event record under its own heading. Fred went back toward the breach with the king.

name: Ed (Hammer Bro)
title: The One Who Remembered Who Builds Switches
status: Historical actor — carried into a side room under Bowser's other arm when the throne-room wall burst, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; placed with the king at the breach thereafter
summary: Ed is the other Hammer Bro under Bowser's arm. The record gives the pair one argument between them and does not split it; the archive files Ed with the half that followed the proposal: Bowser had not built such a switch, so if there was one here somebody might have sabotaged it, old castles contain controls nobody remembers installing, and there was an axe at the end of a river somewhere that this was going to come back to.
description:
The archive keeps Ed as the counterweight — filing, not testimony. The question of who had done the wiring is the one that, a few minutes later, had an answer: a hag, hired by 'a green bean', who could have sworn the switch was the door. Neither Hammer Bro knew that yet. They only knew that a switch nobody remembered installing was a switch somebody else had installed.

He is filed with Fred because the record files them together — two hammers, one argument, carried at a run — and because the argument was the only strategy meeting the garrison held that night. Bowser ended it by refusing the switch and going back to the breach, and Ed went with him.

name: The Supplied Dragon
title: The Contract That Broke the Wall
status: Historical actor — on the castle at the close of the assault record, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; its contract with Fawthful not described as ended
affiliation: Fawthful's Forces (under contract — not loyal; it dislikes the bean)
summary: The dragon is the loud half of Fawthful's assault on Bowser's Castle. Its head cleared the outer wall first; its claw hooked the battlement and shed blocks into the courtyard; it struck the throne-room wall once and failed — 'OWW! My head!' — was asked by Fawthful what kind of incompetent dragon had been supplied, and on the second blow brought the wall in. It speaks Draconic, was sent to kill Bowser, and has said so.
description:
The archive does not have the dragon's name. Fawthful's complaint — that it had been 'supplied', and badly — is the nearest the record comes to describing where it came from, so the archive files it by that word, as it files the Jester by the act and the Koopa Prisoner by the cell.

Two things in the record make it more than weather. The first is the conversation: when a Hammer Bro answered its question in Draconic and argued that he was not the target, the dragon considered the point. It has a bargain with the bean and does not like the bean; it listens to people who speak its language. The second is the apparatus: Fawthful fitted it with a vacuum intake of the same make as the one on his own head, and it used that intake on the Hammer Bro — who got out by shell and spin — and on two red-armband Koopas its wings swept off the building, who did not.

It played with a Goomba in the courtyard until the play stopped being survivable. It held the outer approach while the loyalists went out through the lava tunnel. It was still on the castle when the record ends.

name: The Switch Hag
title: 'I Could Have Sworn It Was the Door'
status: Historical actor — dismissed by Bowser in his own castle, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; whether she left is not recorded
affiliation: Hired by 'a green bean' — contractor, not combatant
summary: Bowser ran into a hag at exactly the wrong moment. She had made a self-destruct switch and was pleased to present it. Asked who had hired her: a green bean. Told the castle was under siege and her duties relinquished, and asked what the switch actually controlled: 'I could have sworn it was the door.' Bowser pushed past her, and the record notes that the switch's true function was never confirmed.
description:
The hag is filed because she is the only person in the record who built part of the castle's downfall and did not know it. Fawthful's forces came in through traitors, doors opened from inside and a dragon; the hag came in through a commission, and left a switch wired into a castle whose owner had not ordered it. The lower command room's own plate — SELF-DESTRUCT over two identical red toggles, with a second label forbidding its use for lighting and a third suggesting one toggle may be the lighting — is filed separately as a prop; whether it is her work the record does not say. Bowser closed that cover without touching either toggle.

She attacked nobody. She is the reason Fred's question about a self-destruct switch had an answer and Bowser's refusal of it had a shape: nobody could say whether the thing destroyed the castle, opened a door, or added another joke to a night already full of them. The archive does not name her; it files her by the switch.

name: Koopa Killer Killa
title: The Boss Nobody Appointed
status: Historical actor — at Toad Town Station with the remnant at the close of the assault record, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; claim to command disputed by at least one Goomba
summary: 'Then the other boss arrived.' Nine Goombas and two Koopas were planning a retreat over an empty train track without their king when Koopa Killer Killa walked in and said that Killa was the boss. A Goomba objected that Killa was not Bowser. Nobody had appointed Killa. The record observes that the empty space left by a retreating king was apparently enough to encourage the claim.
description:
The record gives the name, the claim, and the objection. It does not give which Koopas Killa has killed, whether the title is aspirational, or what Killa intends to do with nine Goombas, two Koopas and a railway with no train on it. The archive files what it has.

Killa is not a traitor and not, in any sense the record recognises, a loyalist. Killa is what grows in the gap between a retreating king and the people he told to meet him at Neo Bowser City: a voice that spoke last. The Goomba who argued, the Hammer Bro behind the door who said no one would be left behind, and the drone that appeared in the next room are the rest of that scene; the archive expects the scene to continue.

name: The Goomba Who Took His Chances
title: He Would Take His Chances
status: Historical actor — walked toward a Fawthful drone at Toad Town Station as the assault record ends, 18 Harvestide 1035 BF; outcome of that walk not yet recorded
summary: The Goomba who watched the dragon talk to a Hammer Bro, ran, and reached the route toward Toad Town Station. He was part of the argument that settled on Toad Town, then Shy Guy Falls, then Toad Town again, in which somebody asked what would happen if Mario came and stepped on them; he objected that Koopa Killer Killa was not Bowser; and when the Hammer Bro behind the door said no one would be left behind, he said he would take his chances. He walked toward the drone. The fight began there.
description:
The archive files him by what he did, because nobody in the record says his name. He is the Goomba who was in the room when Cheeseland was proposed as a stop, on the grounds that one of the Goombas liked cheese. He is the one who told a self-appointed boss that he was not Bowser. He is the one who did not wait to find out whether the drone was alone.

The record ends with his first step toward it. The archive expects to pick him up again on a train, and has left the page open.

name: July Summer Miser
title: The Summer Witch, Founder of the Jul'library, Adept of the Witches Gathering
age: 26 (c. 1014 BF, triplet sister with Jack and Archie)
status: Active — resident scholar and wandering conjurer at Vellanet Rise; founder of the Jul'library; affiliated with the Witches Gathering; maintaining spatial boundary wards across the Midlands margins
affiliation: House Miser / Vellanet Rise, The Witches Gathering, The Jul'library, Independent Scriptorium
summary: July Summer Miser is the second of the five Miser children—born alongside Jack and Archie in the triplet threshold of High Summer—and the arcane anchor of the household. While Jack took to the sword and the Silver Flame's rigid muster roll to feed the cottage, and Archie was consumed by unstable third-eyed pyromancy, July mastered the disciplined geometry of the School of Conjuration. She founded the Jul'library—a roaming repository and scriptorium of bound spaces and extraplanar compendiums based out of Vellanet Rise—and maintains close ties with the Witches Gathering, a loose fellowship of Midlands hedge-scholars and planar herbalists. Patient, sharp-eyed, and carrying the household's emotional weight beneath a tall pointed witch's hat, she commands spatial transposition with clinical precision and keeps an owl familiar named Barnaby watching the tree lines.
description:
Waluigi is adding July Summer Miser to the registry not because House Miser needs another person in a cape, but because somebody in that family had to learn how magic actually works without setting their own eyebrows on fire. Jack has twenty thousand names on a piece of paper; Archie has a hole in the sky and an outstanding arrest warrant in three provinces; July has a staff with a barn owl on top and three bound volumes of spatial geometry that actually balance. WAH. When the arithmetic of a family gets this lopsided, the person who studies conjuration is the only one keeping the walls from falling in.

## The High Summer Triplet and the Hearth

Parish records in the eastern marches are damp, torn, and mostly recorded between crop blights, but the Miser registry is consistent on one point: the eldest three children—Jack, July, and Archie—arrived within hours of each other during the heat wave of 1014 BF. The household called them the Summer Trio until the differences became load-bearing.

When Wanda Miser was keeping five children alive on a labourer's wage, each child developed an emergency response to poverty:
- **Jack** decided the world was an army, enrolled in the Regal Lion muster at fifteen, and ground his way up to knight-commander so the rest of them could eat meat twice a week.
- **Archie** looked inward, found an unstable third eye of bleeding entropy and fire, and decided rules were things other people burned inside of.
- **July** looked at space itself. Space did not require money; it required patience, chalk, and exact angles. She apprenticed herself to local hedge-weavers and hedgewitches along the Midlands border, mastering the transition between provincial folk charms and formal wizardry.

While Jack carried the family's arithmetic and Archie carried its rebellion, July carried its emotional sanity. She was the one who patched torn coats with mending cantrips, mediated between Jack's military curfews and Archie's smoking bedroom floorboards, and kept young Spring and Hark from believing that growing up meant choosing between an iron breastplate and an open flame.

## The School of Conjuration and the Jul'library

Where most wizards of the Midlands gravitate toward the institutional orthodoxy of the Mages' Guild or the aggressive evocation of the war academies, July dedicated her study to the **School of Conjuration** (Wizard Level 7). For July, conjuration is not summoning screaming demons into parlor rooms—it is the art of tethering reality so that distance becomes negotiable.

Her signature creation is the **Jul'library**: an extraplanar and physical scriptorium headquartered in the quiet eastern tower of Vellanet Rise. Part lending library, part sanctuary, and part traveling collection, the Jul'library preserves neglected provincial grimoires, safe planar transit formulas, and non-destructive summoning circles. She is the author and curator of three definitive texts that circulate among Midlands hedge-scholars:
1. *The Jul'library Compendium of Bound Spaces* — A foundational treatise detailing how to summon and dismiss objects and minor beings without leaving planar tears or attracting Canoloths.
2. *Principles of Non-Combustive Conjuration* — Written in dry, clinical prose with thinly veiled exasperation, addressing the dangerous misconception (popularized by her brother Archie) that arcane impact requires burning down the room.
3. *Treatise on Sylvan Circle Traversal* — Detailed field logs documenting the shifting boundaries of peripheral Feywild crossings, boundary stones, and how to bargain with lesser fey without surrendering names or memory.

Her tactical mastery includes **Benign Transposition**—the ability to swap positions in space instantly with an ally or summoned creature—which she uses in the field to pluck wounded allies out of harm's way before hostile blades can connect.

## The Witches Gathering

July is an active adept of the **Witches Gathering**, a decentralized Midlands sisterhood of herbalists, midwives, planar navigators, and boundary-keepers. Unlike the Mages' Guild, which operates under Imperial charters and bureaucratic fees, the Gathering shares knowledge through seasonal moots, coded marginalia, and mutual defense pacts against overzealous inquisitors from Flamekeep.

Through the Gathering, July acts as an arcane diplomat. When local parish priests complain about 'wild witchcraft' in the villages surrounding Vellanet Rise, Jack's knights defer to July. She inspects the wards, certifies the salt lines, and ensures no planar rifts open into the potato fields. In return, the Gathering feeds her intelligence on anomalous regional shifts—including the strange temporal tremors echoing from the deep Feywild.

## Equipment and Familiar

July dresses for travel and work rather than court ceremonies:
- **The Owl Staff**: A seasoned ash quarterstaff topped with a hand-carved barn owl finial. It acts as an arcane focus and a perching rod for **Barnaby**, her summoned celestial owl familiar who scouts tree lines and warns of incoming ambushes.
- **The Field Folio & Messenger Satchel**: A weather-worn leather crossbody satchel enchanted with subtle expansion wards, holding inkstones, vellum, scroll cases, and dried herbs.
- **Witch's Robes & Hat**: A tailored dark-sage duster over heavy traveling wool, belted with brass, and topped with the iconic wide-brimmed conical hat that local villagers recognize from two miles down the road.

## Current Situation: The Unsent Letter

July currently resides at Vellanet Rise, splitting her time between cataloging new acquisitions for the Jul'library, teaching local apprentices, and advising Jack on the metaphysical defenses of his new estate. But the peace is fragile.

Like Jack, July has not been told that Archie is wanted across three planes for catastrophic fires and planar tampering. However, unlike Jack—who reads military dispatches—July reads the astral currents. Her boundary bells in the library have begun ringing unprovoked, tuned to the exact frequency of Feywild temporal distortions. She knows Archie is in deep water; she simply hasn't found the coordinate yet.

## Waluigi's Assessment

*WAH!* A witch who actually files her books on shelves instead of leaving them open in puddles. I respect it! Her brother Jack thinks twenty thousand names on a muster roll makes an army; her brother Archie thinks setting fire to a courthouse is a legal defense; July builds a library and learns how to swap places with people before the ceiling hits them. If the Misers had put her in charge of the family ten years ago, Jack would own half the Midlands and Archie would be running a controlled blast furnace instead of running from interdimensional bailiffs. Watch her staff. The owl doesn't blink, and neither does she.
waluigiComment: July is the only Miser with common sense and a library card. She writes books on how NOT to set things on fire, which should be mandatory reading for her entire family. WAH!

name: Hudston
title: The Toad Who Was Gold By Handshake
status: Active — called out of the TOADALNAEC when the gate toad could not settle a dispute over who owned it; shook Remi's hand, went gold, asked to be shot, enjoyed it, and was counted a toad of the ship's company afterward
summary: Hudston is the toad the gate sent for. He came out on deck, looked at Remi and asked whether she was gold or gold-plated. She offered a handshake as an answer. He went gold from the hand up, asked to be tested, was shot at by Green T, felt the bullet bounce and said it kind of stung but was really fun. The archive has nothing on him before that morning: no rank and no word on what he does aboard the old Vigilance. The spelling is the account's.
description:
## The Toad Who Asked

Hudston is on file for one exchange and one question. The gate toad on the old Vigilance's gangway had a dispute he could not close: a party and a green giant who said the ship was theirs, against a ship that a Speaker had already claimed. He called for Hudston, and Hudston came out on deck.

His first words were about Remi. He asked whether she was gold or only gold-plated. She answered by shaking his hand. The gold ran up his arm and across him, and the first thing he did with a new body was invite everyone to test it. Green T shot at him against the wall. The bullet glanced away. Hudston said it stung and he had enjoyed it, and asked how he could ever repay her.

The Toads on deck told Remi she was one of them. The archive files Hudston as the first of several to go gold.
waluigiComment: A toad asked a stranger whether she was gold or gold-plated and was told to find out for himself. Waluigi has been trying to give that answer to a customs officer for years. WAH.
